frequency_question: What proportion of bilateral technical treaty renewals successfully complete all procedural drafting and signing steps within a 132-day window from the initiation of the final renewal phase?
membership_rule: Includes all formal intergovernmental resource-sharing treaty extensions or renewals that required joint technical committee review, legal drafting, and executive sign-off. Excludes unilateral terminations or treaties where negotiation was abandoned prior to drafting.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty Permanent Indus Commission annual renewals and technical adjustments
U.S.-Mexico Water Treaty Minute adoption process
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II protocol extension
Senegal River Basin Development Organization charter protocol renewal

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named; representative of major formalized transboundary water protocol renewals.
known_gaps: Does not account for rare instances where negotiations stall indefinitely prior to the signing phase, which are excluded by definition since this aperture assumes full cooperation and focuses purely on the clock.
skeleton: 6 historical instances of bilateral water resource agreement renewals/protocols completed under compressed administrative timelines.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 enumerated comparable structured bureaucratic processes where mechanical time allowances matched the available calendar window.
validity_reason: Bureaucratic and diplomatic protocols for treaty drafting and signing timelines remain stable across decades unless major administrative overhauls occur.
